analysis.title: Marketcolour + Earnings (Ioannis Blekos, 28 Oct 2026)
key_insights: US equities closed higher Tuesday: SPX +60bps to 7722 (6 of 11 sectors up, Tech +1.49%, Energy -2.20%), NDX +129bps to 29651 (first back-to-back 1%+ gain in 3 months), RTY +116bps to 2818.
AI trade showed more signs of stabilization: GS Data Centers basket +4.21% and AI Semis basket +3.10% both outperformed.
In Europe, Semis (+5.4%), EU Miners (+2.4%) and Housebuilders (+2.3%) outperformed, helped by gilt yield stabilisation.

FOMC preview: market pricing of the Fed path has removed one hike and now peaks at just over 4.5%. GS baseline and probability-weighted Fed forecasts are considerably less hawkish, because GS doubts the FOMC will hike four times and expects cuts later.

Historical pattern around the first hike of a cycle: equities tend to struggle initially then recover quickly, yields rise into the first hike and keep rising after it (more in larger cycles), the curve keeps flattening, and the real trade-weighted USD tends to strengthen into the hike with mixed results afterwards.

Pension rebalancing: an estimated $9bn to sell ranks in the 50th percentile of all buy and sell estimates by absolute dollar value over the past three years and the 65th percentile since January 2000.

Momentum is recovering (+2.5%) after a ~20% drawdown over the last few weeks. High-beta momentum (GSPRHIMO) is up ~8% over the last 3 sessions. Global fundamental long/short momentum exposure is near YTD lows after the recent de-grossing.

SK Hynix (+11%) reported revenue of 104tr won ($78bn, +328% y/y) vs consensus 98tr won and operating profit of 88tr won vs consensus 76tr won. It plans to return up to $75bn to investors, has long-term agreements with 14 major customers covering over 50% of 2027-2028 capacity, and expects memory demand to outpace supply through 2030.

Reckitt (Buy, PT GBP6.5, 20% upside): GS expects Q4 acceleration as headwinds fade and cold/flu expectations rise, with Core Reckitt at +6.3%, implying +3.8% organic sales growth in FY26 and +4.9% in FY27E.

BASF Q3 adjusted EBITDA beat by 10%, driven by all divisions except Agri Solutions and by lower corporate costs. Volumes were weaker than expected but price realisation held up better in upstream divisions. EBITDA guidance was raised by 100m at the top end. The guide still implies a slowdown in Q4. The FCF guide is unchanged despite the higher EBITDA guide and a 400m lower capex guide.

ASM International: Q3 revenue beat by 5% and gross profit by 6%. Q4 2026 revenue guided to about EUR1.23bn +/-5% at constant currency (+3% vs consensus at midpoint). 2027 revenue guided above EUR5.7bn at constant currency, 5% ahead of consensus and up from the EUR3.7-4.6bn range given at the CMD.

Dassault Systemes (DSY): GS says the headlines look better than the underlying picture. The Q3 beat (revenue +2% vs expectations) was driven by licences, and the raised full-year guidance largely reflects the inclusion of ArisGlobal. The stock has rallied strongly. The next catalyst is the CMD on 17 November.

BNP Paribas: net profit beat by 7%, driven by a 2% top-line beat (better Equities) and in-line costs. A EUR1.3bn buyback was announced, with possibly more at full year. Provisions are 8% higher but similar to the prior quarter, and cost of risk was stable at 40bps. Stock up 2-3%.

Kone Q3 was light: orders +5.5% in line (Schindler's were above +10%), sales growth 3.4% vs consensus 5%, adjusted EBIT a 2% miss with margins in line. Guidance raised at the low end (sales growth 4-6% from 3-6%, margin 12.5-12.9% from 12.3-13%). GS reads this as consistent with Schindler gaining share and large orders at Kone's expense.

Saint-Gobain: slight miss on Q3 organic growth (France especially weak). Americas were helped by roofing, against industry volumes of -13%, but this looks temporary because the company flagged a deterioration in Q4 organic growth with US destocking and continuing pressures.

market_movers.rationale: Reckitt: GS expects Q4 acceleration into FY27 as headwinds fade, with Core Reckitt at +6.3% and FY26 organic growth of +3.8%. Reckitt has no liquid US listing, so no ticker.

earnings_insights: SK Hynix reported revenue 104tr won ($78bn, +328% y/y) vs consensus 98tr won, and operating profit 88tr won vs consensus 76tr won. Already printed.
BASF Q3 adjusted EBITDA reported 10% above consensus. Top end of EBITDA guide raised by 100m, capex guide lowered by 400m, FCF guide unchanged. Already printed.

ASM International Q3 reported revenue 5% above consensus and gross profit 6% above. Q4 2026 guide about EUR1.23bn +/-5% at constant currency (+3% vs consensus at midpoint). 2027 guide above EUR5.7bn at constant currency (5% above consensus).
Dassault Systemes Q3 revenue reported 2% above expectations, driven by licences. The raised full-year guidance largely reflects the ArisGlobal inclusion. CMD on 17 November.
BNP Paribas reported net profit 7% above consensus, top line 2% above, costs in line, provisions 8% higher, cost of risk 40bps. EUR1.3bn buyback announced.

Kone Q3 reported orders +5.5% (in line), sales growth 3.4% vs consensus 5%, adjusted EBIT 2% below consensus. FY guidance: sales growth 4-6% (from 3-6%), margin 12.5-12.9% (from 12.3-13%). Consensus sits at +5.2% growth and 12.6% margin.
Saint-Gobain Q3 organic growth slightly below expectations, with France weak and Americas helped by roofing. Q4 organic growth flagged to deteriorate.
Reckitt (GS estimate): Core Reckitt +6.3% in Q4E, FY26 organic sales growth +3.8%, FY27E +4.9%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing has removed one hike from the expected path. GS expects a less hawkish path than the market, with fewer hikes and cuts later.

risk_factors: A faster or larger Fed hiking cycle than GS expects (market pricing peaks above 4.5%).
Historically, equities struggle initially after the first hike and yields keep rising in larger hiking cycles.
Saint-Gobain flagged Q4 deterioration with US destocking, and BASF guidance implies a Q4 slowdown.
Dassault's beat was licence-driven and the guidance uplift reflects an acquisition, so the quality of the beat is in question.
vol_and_positioning: Momentum is up +2.5% after a ~20% drawdown over recent weeks. High-beta momentum (GSPRHIMO) is up ~8% over the last 3 sessions.
Global fundamental long/short momentum exposure is near YTD lows after the recent de-grossing episode.
Pension rebalancing: $9bn to sell, 50th percentile over the past three years and 65th percentile since January 2000.
